newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE WINS, HILL SET THE PACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE WINS, HILL SET THE PACE.

text.p: World champion Damon Hill came within seconds of a remarkable victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday before last lap mechanical trouble handed Jacques Villeneuve the spoils.
The Canadian's win trimmed Michael Schumacher's lead over Villeneuve in the world drivers' championship to just three points with six races remaining.
Schumacher has 56 points, Villeneuve 53.

Villeneuve, in his Williams, took the lead for the first and only time in the 77-lap race on the final lap after Hill, whose previously troublesome Arrows had surprisingly dominated the race, slowed down because of hydraulic problems.
These hit his throttle and gearbox and made it impossible for him to do anything else but cruise towards the line.
The Briton held on for second place -- ending the Arrows team's long search for a good result -- ahead of compatriot Johnny Herbert in a Sauber.
Former world champion Schumacher of Germany finished fourth for Ferrari ahead of his 22-year-old younger brother Ralf in a Jordan and Japan's Shinji Nakano in a Prost.
In the constructors' title race, Ferrari have 74 points and Williams, the defending champions, have 72.
For most of the massive crowd, disappointment in not seeing Hill claim a well-deserved and memorable victory was the overwhelming feeling at the end of the day.
Hill, starting from third on the grid, took second place at the opening corner and stayed there for 10 laps.
At the start of the 11th, Hill sensed that Schumacher's tyres were wearing badly and shot past him on the inside of the corner at the end of the straight to take the lead.
Apart from five laps when Germany's Heinz-Harald Frentzen, in his Williams, took over after the first flurry of pit-stops, Hill stayed in command until the final lap.

Frentzen was unlucky because he looked dominant and clocked the fastest lap of the race before being brought to a halt by a fuel-nozzle problem. The malfunction caused a fire at the rear of his car and his race ended in the pits.
Hill said: "I was getting to the point when I began to think the race was there to win when everything went wrong, but that is typical of Formula One.

"I was very disappointed, but I was pleased that the car went so well and that we were so competitive. It would have been the first win for Arrows, for Yamaha and for Bridgestone, but it was not to be.
"It was one of those things that you just cannot control. I was lucky really to get to the finish. It could have been better, but it could have been a lot worse."
Villeneuve's win was his fifth this year and the ninth of his brief Formula One career, but he admitted that Hill deserved real praise for his efforts.
As soon as he climbed from his car, he ran across to congratulate and commiserate with his former team-mate.
"Damon was really flying, he was very fast and I just couldn't get near him," admitted Villeneuve.
"I wanted to, but I thought he would not be able to finish so I stayed there and watched and waited. Then I began to worry that he would finish.

"Someone came on the radio from the pits and told me he was slowing down and that was when I began to push right at the end. I went wide on the grass when I passed him because I was worried he had a suspension problem."
Villeneuve added: "It was amazing to see him up there with us at the front. He really deserved to win today."
Schumacher said that "I hoped Hill would win today as he deserved to and also because it would have helped me in the championship. I must congratulate him and the his team on the job they did.
"At the end of the race, my brother was faster than me and if we had not been fighting for the championship, I would have let him pass."
Hill was not the only victim of the last lap melodrama as Schumacher's team-mate Briton Eddie Irvine was pushed out of sixth place following a collision with Nakano.
"We all had to brake hard," he said. "We were following Michael and Ralf, but Nakano did not manage to stop in time and ran into me."
